A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Watch & Learn with the same authors, core framework, and substantial shared experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original IDM labeling evaluations, OSWorld ICL and fine-tuning results, ablations, and appendix data-scaling and application-level analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original OSWorld experiments and adds WindowsAgentArena results, a revised IDM labeling evaluation, and additional trajectory examples.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 expands the action vocabulary from five primitives to six by adding Release and defining Click as a press event, enabling compositional drag-and-drop previously described as unsupported. Coordinate bins change from 0–1000 to 0–999. The core IDM, retrieval, and ICL/SFT pipeline remains intact; most appendix architecture additions are newly disclosed details.

E1.justification: v2 adds WindowsAgentArena, extending downstream evaluation beyond Ubuntu-based OSWorld to Windows workflows. It also removes Mind2Web from the reported IDM training and evaluation coverage, using autonomous web transitions instead. The application inventory replaces Affinity Designer with Gimp.

E2.justification: The new WindowsAgentArena comparison includes OpenCUA-7B and UltraCUA-7B, neither evaluated in v1. Existing OSWorld comparator membership is retained. UI-TARS-1.5-7B is not a newly introduced model: v1 already identifies that version in its experimental setup.

E3.justification: The reported IDM corpus changes from roughly 500K synthetic plus 132K Mind2Web transitions to approximately 600K synthetic transitions. The Mind2Web labeling test is replaced by a balanced holdout containing 100 transitions for each of six action types. WindowsAgentArena introduces a 15-step evaluation protocol; OSWorld retains its 50-step limit.

E4.justification: Tables 10–27 add detailed GIMP labeling, OSWorld VLC, and Windows File Explorer trajectory case studies. Appendix D.1 also briefly reports a qualitative NaFlex-versus-fixed-resolution comparison. The existing action/reasoning, retrieval, data-scaling, and application-domain analyses remain substantially unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's specified labeling-test sample size changes evaluation design, not uncertainty reporting; its discussion of predictive probabilities does not add a statistical evaluation.

E6.justification: New WindowsAgentArena results report 24.0% for W&L fine-tuning versus 18.1% without fine-tuning, 12.9% with TongUI labels, 13.5% for OpenCUA-7B, and 21.7% for UltraCUA-7B. Table 4 replaces labeling results and adds Release: W&L action accuracy is 91.6% on v1's Mind2Web test and 91.7% on v2's different holdout, not a comparable performance gain. Existing OSWorld results and retained appendix numerical analyses are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies mathematical mappings for the previously underspecified action and coordinate heads and visual cross-attention in Equations 1–4. Appendix E largely formalizes the existing cross-entropy training description. This is a limited addition of mathematical definitions, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add a bounded state-of-the-art claim for 7B-scale models on WindowsAgentArena under a 15-step limit, and the conclusion explicitly claims generalization across operating systems. The central contributions—video-to-trajectory labeling and benefits for both ICL and supervised training—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the drag-and-drop and scrolling-data limitations with unsupported hotkeys, arguing that graphical alternatives preserve broad functional coverage. It adds an explanation linking TongUI's weaker Windows agent performance to noisier supervision and contrasts this with W&L's cross-platform reliability. Existing retrieval and data-scaling interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendices C–E add detailed Playwright collection and filtering rules, viewport, worker counts, runtime, full ICL prompts, encoder preprocessing, Transformer dimensions, head parameterization, and loss weighting. These substantially extend v1's coarse implementation description. Some new disclosures remain inconsistent: Appendix D calls the encoder frozen, while Appendix E says the entire model is trained end-to-end.

R1.justification: v2 adds an OpenCUA/AgentNet annotation-cost comparison and references WindowsAgentArena, UltraCUA, Agent S/S2, agent-scaling work, and SigLIP-2. These update context and competitive positioning while preserving the main distinction between dedicated inverse-dynamics labeling and prior MLLM-based synthesis.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and data-synthesis related work undergo extensive rewriting. v2 merges the separate ICL/SFT method subsections, reorganizes experimental setup and analysis, and restructures the appendices with dedicated architecture and training sections. The earlier LLM-use disclosure appendix is removed.

P2.justification: v2 redraws and crops Figure 2, adds the Windows results table, expands the labeling table with Release, and introduces extensive screenshot-and-action tables plus ICL prompt boxes. Table captions move above tables, and several displays are relocated or reordered. Figures 1 and 3 retain their underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: The Windows evaluation and substantially expanded collection, model, and prompt documentation improve empirical breadth and reproducibility beyond v1. The benefit is tempered by replacing the independent Mind2Web labeling test with a same-pipeline holdout and by inconsistencies in the new documentation, including frozen versus end-to-end encoder training and incompatible image/patch dimensions. These limits prevent the revision from establishing a substantial overall quality improvement.
